newsitem.title: SRI LANKA: Shortage drives Colombo rubber prices higher.
newsitem.headline: Shortage drives Colombo rubber prices higher.

text.p: Rubber prices rose at the Colombo auction on Thursday because very little was on sale due to drought, exporters said.
"The market was very firm," one said. "There was hardly any good quality rubber available but there was interest all round."
Prices could rise further in the weeks ahead because of the shortage caused by lack of water to run factories, he added.
Other exporters said prices were likely to stay strong because tapping would be disrupted by the April 13-14 traditional new year celebrations.
Brokers said 142 tonnes of crepe, 64 tonnes of scrap crepe and 28 tonnes of sheet were on offer.

Best latex one-x, the purest grade, rose to 78 rupees per kg from 77.75 rupees last Thursday, brokers said. Latex crepe number one rose to 77.50 from 77.25 while RSS 1 went for 61 rupees after being unquoted last week.
Sri Lanka is experiencing drought after the November-March northeast monsoon failed for a second year in a row.
